newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures tumble late on stops, close weaker.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures tumble late on stops, close weaker.

text.p: CME hog futures fell when general long liquidation sparked fund selling and touched off sell stops late, traders. Pork bellies were pressured by a weaker cash belly market, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.900 cent per lb lower to 0.175 higher with April pacing the setback and ending at 73.175 cents. Pork bellies finished 0.725 to 1.225 cents lower with May off 1.175 at 81.375 cents.
Hog futures tumbled late when early short covering subsided and liquidation, partly linked to higher corn futures, touched off sell stops, traders said.

Hog futures had shown early gains on firmer-than-expected cash hog prices Tuesday and short covering, thought to be unwinding of short hog/long live cattle spreads. But the covering stopped at the same time grain futures rallied and cash pork products were reported easier. The premium of futures to cash also loomed large, they said.
"They are having a hard time keeping the premium on the board on the hogs," said Karl Skold, Director of Research for Frontier Risk Management.
